# EXPERIMENT DESIGN — Effect of Runtime-Quantization Clipping Ratio on PPL (LLaMA2-7B, symmetric input + asymmetric KV-cache quantization)

Design document only. No experiment has been run; nothing below is a result.

## 1. Objective
Determine how the clipping ratio r used during inference-time quantization affects perplexity on LLaMA2-7B when activations are quantized symmetrically and the KV cache is quantized asymmetrically, and identify the optimal FIXED clipping ratio that best balances quantization error against model accuracy. Two sub-objectives: (a) characterize PPL as a function of r; (b) isolate how much of the PPL change is attributable to the input (activation) channel versus the KV-cache channel.

## 2. Setup
- Model: LLaMA2-7B, base (non-chat) weights, FP16 reference. Fixed for all conditions.
- Quantization type: runtime (inference-time) dynamic quantization of activations and KV cache (not post-training weight quant).
- Clipping-ratio definition (ASSUMPTION A1): r is the threshold-to-max ratio. For a tensor x, clip_threshold = r · max(|x|), r ∈ (0,1]. The quantizer's effective range is derived from the clipped threshold instead of the raw max. r = 1.0 ⇒ threshold = max ⇒ no clipping (full range). r < 1.0 ⇒ outliers beyond ±threshold are clipped (saturated), which shrinks the scale and increases per-step resolution for inliers at the cost of saturating the tail. This is the single scalar swept in the experiment.
- Input/activation channel (Channel I): SYMMETRIC affine quantization, zero-point 0. Scale s_in = (r·max|x_in|) / 2^(b_in−1); quantize Q = clamp(round(x_in/s_in), −2^(b_in−1), 2^(b_in−1)−1).
- KV-cache channel (Channel K): ASYMMETRIC affine quantization. Per-tensor (min, max) (ASSUMPTION A3), both clipped by r: eff_max = min(raw_max, r·|max deviation|) and eff_min = max(raw_min, −r·|min deviation|) applied symmetrically about the tensor's extreme magnitudes; scale s_kv = (eff_max − eff_min)/(2^b_kv − 1), zero-point 0; quantize Q = clamp(round((x−eff_min)/s_kv), 0, 2^b_kv−1). (Per-head / per-channel (min,max) is a robustness variant, see Limitations.)
- Bit widths (CHOSEN VALUE, ASSUMPTION A4): PRIMARY condition = 8-bit symmetric input (b_in = 8) + 4-bit asymmetric KV cache (b_kv = 4). Rationale: 4-bit KV is the regime where KV-cache quantization is actually motivated in practice and where clipping has a visible effect, while 8-bit inputs keep activation error low so the KV channel dominates the signal. SENSITIVITY: repeat the C2 and C3 sweeps at b_kv = 3 to check robustness of the optimal-r conclusion.
- Quantizer identity (ASSUMPTION A2): generic affine dynamic quantizer (PyTorch-dynamic-quant style) with the scale driven by r. NOT SmoothQuant (no outlier-migration smoothing) and NOT GPTQ.

## 3. Factorial Design
Swept factor: r ∈ {1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3} (8 levels, 0.1 steps). All other factors (model, bit widths, eval) held constant so r is the sole varied factor within a condition.

Conditions (each swept over all 8 r-levels):
- C1 (input-only): Channel I quantized (symmetric, 8-bit, ratio r); KV cache kept in FP16. Isolates the input channel.
- C2 (KV-only): Channel K quantized (asymmetric, 4-bit, ratio r); inputs kept in FP16. Isolates the KV-cache channel.
- C3 (both / actual scenario): both channels quantized at the same shared ratio r (ASSUMPTION A5). This is the configuration the question describes.

Controls:
- CTRL-A (accuracy upper bound): full FP16, no quantization. Single model-level evaluation → PPL_ref.
- CTRL-B (no-clip quantization reference): C3 evaluated at r = 1.0 (no clipping). This is a point on the C3 curve, not a separate run. It isolates pure quantization overhead from clipping: ΔPPL(C3@r=1.0 − PPL_ref) is the "no-clip" cost; any dip below it at r<1.0 is the clipping benefit; the rise at very low r is over-clipping.

Distinct PPL evaluations: C1 (8) + C2 (8) + C3 (8) + CTRL-A (1) = 25 (CTRL-B is C3@r=1.0, already counted). This is within the ~32-eval ballpark used for the feasibility estimate.

## 4. Evaluation Protocol
- Primary dataset: WikiText-2 (test split) — matches LLaMA2's own reported-PPL convention.
- Secondary (robustness): C4 validation split, same harness.
- Harness (ASSUMPTION A8): max_length = 2048 tokens; ~500 evaluation samples; sliding-window stride = 128; perplexity = exp(mean cross-entropy) over the log-likelihood of each next token, averaged over all valid samples/windows. Same tokenization and preprocessing as the LLaMA2 reference for comparability.
- Auxiliary (quantization error, offline): for each r and channel, capture representative activations / KV tensors across a fixed calibration batch, and compute (i) per-tensor MSE between dequantized and original values, and (ii) SNR = 10·log10(‖x‖²/‖x−x̂‖²). Also record the fraction of elements actually clipped at each r, to directly tie the r-grid to the clipping mechanism. These error metrics are reported to explain the PPL curve, not as the primary metric.
- Context note: 2048-token context is used for PPL; if KV-cache pressure is the intended regime, a longer-context PPL (e.g., 4096) may be added as a robustness check (see Limitations).

## 5. Analysis Plan
- PPL curves: plot PPL(r) for C1, C2, C3 (and 3-bit-KV variants) against r, with CTRL-A (PPL_ref) and CTRL-B (C3@r=1.0) marked as references.
- Expected shape: non-monotonic (U- or J-shaped). At r=1.0, full range ⇒ coarsest resolution, no clipping. At moderate r, the reduced scale improves inlier resolution and can lower error. At very low r, too many elements are saturated ⇒ error rises. The PPL minimum is the operating trade-off point.
- Error curves: plot MSE(r) and SNR(r) per channel, plus fraction-clipped(r); correlate the PPL minimum with the error minimum to confirm the resolution-gain-vs-outlier-loss mechanism.
- Optimal-r extraction: r* = argmin_r PPL(r) in C3 (the joint scenario); report r* per channel from C1 and C2 as well, to see whether the per-channel optima agree with the joint optimum.
- Budget criterion (directly operationalises "balances quantization error and model accuracy"): define a permissible accuracy loss Δ = 0.1 PPL (default). Report r_budget = smallest r (most aggressive) such that PPL(r) ≤ PPL_ref + Δ, in both C3 and per-channel. This gives the most compression that still meets the accuracy budget, alongside the pure argmin.
- Per-channel attribution: decompose ΔPPL(C3) ≈ ΔPPL(C1) + ΔPPL(C2) (additivity check). Report the fraction of total PPL degradation attributable to the input channel vs. the KV channel at each r, identifying which channel the clipping ratio most affects.
- Boundary-refinement note: if the argmin (or the budget boundary) falls on a grid edge (e.g., r = 0.3 or r = 1.0), a follow-up finer sweep (0.05 steps within a ±0.1 window around that boundary) would be warranted to localize the optimum — a standard refinement, not a new experiment.

## 6. Feasibility & Resources
- Hardware: a single A100-80G (or equivalent) suffices for LLaMA2-7B inference with modified KV-cache and activation quantization hooks. No distributed/multi-GPU setup required.
- Scope: ~25 distinct PPL evaluations (within the ~32-eval ballpark): 8 r-levels × 3 conditions = 24, + 1 FP16 baseline; the r=1.0 no-clip control is a C3 point. Each PPL evaluation at 2048 context on WikiText-2 is on the order of ~20–40 min. Estimated total wall-clock on one GPU is in the ballpark of 10–20 hours. This is a feasibility estimate, not a committed runtime.
- Software: LLaMA2-7B weights plus a vLLM/transformers inference path with custom hooks to (a) apply symmetric clipping to activations and (b) apply asymmetric clipping to the KV cache at the specified bit widths; a standard PPL harness; offline capture of activations/KV for the error metrics.
- This environment (CPU-only, no network, no weights, no preinstalled deps) cannot execute the design; feasibility above is for the intended target environment.

## 7. Assumptions & Limitations
- A1 (ASSUMPTION, chosen): clipping ratio r = threshold-to-max ratio, clip_threshold = r·max|x|, r ∈ (0,1], r=1.0 = no clip. No source document was available to confirm; alternative definitions (fraction of clipped elements, percentile threshold) would change the factor levels.
- A2 (ASSUMPTION): generic affine dynamic quantizer; NOT SmoothQuant or GPTQ. A smoothing-based or PTQ method would alter the clipping mechanism and results.
- A3 (ASSUMPTION): KV-cache asymmetric affine is per-tensor (min,max). Per-head or per-channel (min,max) is a robustness variant that could shift the optimal r.
- A4 (CHOSEN VALUE, ASSUMPTION): 8-bit symmetric input + 4-bit asymmetric KV cache as the primary condition; 3-bit KV as a sensitivity/robustness check. The optimal r is bit-width-dependent, so conclusions are scoped to these widths.
- A5 (ASSUMPTION): a single shared r is applied to both channels in C3, matching the singular "the clipping ratio" in the brief. Independent per-channel ratios would make C3 a 2D sweep (r_in × r_kv) and the "optimal fixed ratio" a pair.
- A6 (ASSUMPTION): the "fixed" (vs. dynamic) ratio is motivated by determinism and a cheap, precomputable threshold that avoids per-tensor max/percentile computation at inference time; the specific inference-time memory constraint is not confirmed. If the true motivation is a hard KV memory/throughput budget, the optimality criterion should be tied to that budget rather than pure PPL.
- A7 (FIXED BY BRIEF, not an assumption): inputs quantized symmetrically, KV cache quantized asymmetrically.
- A8 (ASSUMPTION): PPL eval uses 2048 context, ~500 samples, stride 128 (LLaMA2 convention), not stated in the brief.
- A9: design-only; NOT executable in this environment (no GPU, no weights, no network). No experiment has been run and none is claimed; the deliverable is this design document.

Additional limitations: (i) PPL at 2048 context may not reflect the long-context KV-cache pressure that motivates KV quantization — a longer-context PPL is a recommended robustness check; (ii) the additivity decomposition in the analysis is an approximation (channels interact); (iii) a single model size (7B) limits generalizability to other LLaMA2 sizes.
